endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: Commure, as another example, is in the process of cocreating clinical “nudges” with health system partners to enable AI-driven reminders at the point of care, based on data captured in ambient notes and from EHR metadata.

endorsements.title: Barriers and opportunities of scaling ambient AI scribes for clinical documentation across diverse healthcare settings
endorsements.quote: Ambient scribes need to adapt to local vernacular by contextual training and customization.

evidence.title: A Novel Playbook for Pragmatic Trial Operations to Monitor and Evaluate Ambient Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Recovery of ICD-10 documentation accuracy after template redesign and user training
evidence.effect: Template redesign combined with user training restored accuracy to baseline after a decline from 79% (95% CI, 72 to 86%) to 35% (95% CI, 28 to 42%); separate intervention effects were not reported.
evidence.quote: A brief workflow issue related to a note template change initially reduced ICD-10 documentation accuracy from 79% (95% confidence interval [CI], 72 to 86%) to 35% (95% CI, 28 to 42%); accuracy returned to baseline after note template redesign and user training.

evidence.title: Nurse-Led Ambient AI Scribe for Patient Safety Incident Investigation Reports (Project NARRATE): Retrospective Pre-Post Comparative Document-Quality Study
evidence.outcome: Completeness and narrative quality of locally tailored ambient-scribe investigation reports
evidence.effect: Voluntary pre-post comparison: completeness adjusted difference 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001); adapted PDQI difference 0.53 (95% CI 0.37-0.69; P<.001). Results concern the bundled workflow; template-specific effects were not isolated.
evidence.quote: Unadjusted mean WHO total completeness was 11.81 (SD 3.39) for conventional reports and 13.61 (SD 2.54) for NARRATE reports; the unadjusted difference was 1.80 points, and the cluster-adjusted mean difference was 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001).

evidence.title: Impact of an Ambient AI Scribe on Medical Student Objective Structured Clinical Examination Notes: Nonrandomized Clinical Trial
evidence.effect: Chief complaint scores declined because AI notes often omitted symptom duration, a locally required criterion for full credit.
evidence.quote: The difference in chief complaint scores was likely due to conciseness in AI notes that often omitted symptom duration, an explicit criterion for full credit on QNOTE.

commentary.bottom_line: Two real-deployment studies found better documentation after locally tailored templates, but each bundled template changes with training or workflow changes, so the template effect alone is unknown. The certainty that collaborative template customization by itself improves ambient scribe notes is very low.

perspectives.view: The US study of 66 providers used a quasi-experimental design. The Singapore study compared 150 investigation reports before and after the change without a comparator. Neither study isolated the template component, and supervisor investigation reports are indirect evidence for clinical notes. Risk of bias, indirectness, and bundled interventions lower certainty to very low.

In a simulated study of 104 medical students, chief complaint scores fell because AI notes often omitted symptom duration, a locally required element. This shows that generic formats can drop required content. It does not show that customization prevents such omissions, and no study linked template changes to patient harm or near misses.

In one deployment, ICD-10 documentation accuracy fell from 79% (95% CI, 72 to 86%) to 35% (95% CI, 28 to 42%). It returned to baseline after template redesign combined with user training. The recovery suggests that local redesign may work in live workflows. Because training accompanied the redesign, the template's separate contribution cannot be estimated.

A locally tailored ambient scribe workflow was associated with higher report completeness (adjusted difference 1.95, 95% CI 0.91 to 3.00). It was also associated with higher adapted PDQI scores (difference 0.53, 95% CI 0.37 to 0.69). Participation was voluntary, which may have selected motivated users.

Both deployments paired customization with other work, including user training at one site and a bundled workflow change at the other. The study summaries do not report staff time, vendor effort, or cost. Administrators therefore have no data on the resources that collaborative customization requires or how it scales across specialties.

commentary.research_gap: No study has compared customized with generic ambient scribe templates while holding training and workflow constant. No study has measured the cost of customization or linked template changes to omissions that reach patients.
commentary.underserved_note: Neither test reported including Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. It is unknown whether locally customized templates capture content these patients need, such as interpreter use or social needs, or whether the reported gains would hold in those settings.
